findings.description: With None as value, the current Python comparison raises TypeError; if non-numeric inputs are invalid, assert that exception.
findings.recommendation: Add an exception test for None to document the input contract and prevent silent coercion assumptions.

findings.title: Recommend boundary acceptance test
findings.description: The inclusive range check should accept exact endpoints 1 and 65535 and return them unchanged.
findings.recommendation: Add a parameterized pytest case for both valid endpoints.

findings.title: Recommend out-of-range rejection test
findings.description: Values below 1 and above 65535 should raise ValueError with message 'invalid port'.
findings.recommendation: Parameterize invalid boundary-adjacent and negative values.

findings.title: Recommend numeric-string input test
findings.description: parse_port converts values with int(), so decimal string inputs should parse to integers.
findings.recommendation: Add a parameterized test showing numeric strings round-trip correctly.

findings.title: Recommend empty and non-numeric string test
findings.description: Malformed strings reach int() and should raise ValueError before range validation runs.
findings.recommendation: Add a parameterized malformed-string exception test.

findings.title: Recommend None input test
findings.description: int(None) raises TypeError, so None currently bypasses the explicit ValueError path; confirm whether uniform rejection is intended.
findings.recommendation: Add a test pinning the None behavior.
suggested_tests: test_parse_port_none_input: inputs=None; expected=TypeError under current int() behavior

findings.title: Recommend an empty-sequence test
findings.description: Calling first_item with an empty list reaches items[0] with no elements; current behavior is an IndexError. Test should pin whether that propagation is intended.
findings.recommendation: Add a test asserting the empty-list behavior explicitly.

findings.title: Recommend a None-input test
findings.description: Passing None as items causes subscripting on None, raising TypeError. Verify the documented/expected failure mode rather than an accidental one.
findings.recommendation: Test None input and assert the exception type.

findings.title: Recommend a happy-path first-element test
findings.description: Core behavior returns index 0; test both list and tuple with multiple elements to confirm first element and index-0 semantics.
findings.recommendation: Parameterize over list and tuple inputs.
suggested_tests: test_returns_first_element: inputs=items=[10,20,30] and (10,20,30); expected=10 for both

findings.title: Recommend a non-indexable iterable test
findings.description: Sets and generators are iterable but not subscriptable, so they raise TypeError; this clarifies the accepted input types.
findings.recommendation: Test a set or generator input and assert TypeError.

findings.title: Recommend a single-element boundary test
findings.description: The smallest non-empty sequence is a boundary worth pinning; also consider a string input, which currently returns its first character (intent uncertain).
findings.recommendation: Cover the one-element boundary and document string behavior.
suggested_tests: test_single_element_and_string: inputs=items=[42] then 'ab'; expected=42 then 'a' (current behavior, intent unconfirmed)

findings.title: Recommend a nonexistent-path test
findings.description: load_text delegates directly to open, so a path that does not exist propagates FileNotFoundError. Pin this contract so callers can rely on it.
findings.recommendation: Add a test passing a path in a temp directory that does not exist and assert FileNotFoundError.

findings.title: Recommend an empty-file test
findings.description: An empty file yields read()'s empty string; confirm the function returns '' rather than None for zero-byte input.
findings.recommendation: Create an empty temp file and assert the return value equals the empty string.
suggested_tests: test_load_text_empty_file: inputs=path to zero-byte utf-8 file; expected=returns ''

findings.title: Recommend a non-UTF-8 bytes test
findings.description: Encoding is hardcoded to utf-8, so files with bytes invalid in UTF-8 fail during read. Verify the exception type surfaced to callers.
findings.recommendation: Write raw bytes such as b'\xff\xfe' to a temp file and assert UnicodeDecodeError is raised on read.
suggested_tests: test_load_text_invalid_utf8: inputs=file containing b'\xff\xfe'; expected=raises UnicodeDecodeError

findings.title: Recommend a directory-path test
findings.description: Passing a directory to open raises IsADirectoryError; confirming propagation documents behavior for misused arguments.
findings.recommendation: Pass a temporary directory path and assert IsADirectoryError.

findings.title: Recommend a None-path test
findings.description: A None or non-string path is passed straight to open with no validation; verify the resulting TypeError is the observed behavior.
findings.recommendation: Call load_text(None) and assert TypeError is raised.

findings.title: Recommend boundary tests for 0 and 100 percent
findings.description: The inclusive range check allows percent values 0 and 100; these boundaries should be exercised because they produce no discount and full discount.
findings.recommendation: Add a parameterized boundary test covering percent 0 and percent 100.
suggested_tests: test_discount_percent_boundaries: inputs=price=100, percent=0 and price=100, percent=100; expected=100.0 and 0.0

findings.title: Recommend out-of-range percent exception tests
findings.description: Percent values below 0 or above 100 reach the explicit ValueError branch; test both sides of the valid range and exception message.
findings.recommendation: Add tests asserting ValueError and the message for percent -1 and 101.
suggested_tests: test_discount_percent_out_of_range: inputs=price=100, percent=-1 and price=100, percent=101; expected=ValueError('invalid percent')

findings.title: Recommend a non-numeric percent type test
findings.description: Passing None or a string to the chained comparison raises TypeError before the explicit ValueError branch; document the expected exception type for malformed input.
findings.recommendation: Add a test with percent=None and assert TypeError.

findings.title: Recommend a two-decimal rounding test
findings.description: The result is rounded to two decimal places; a case whose intermediate value has more decimals verifies the rounding behavior.
findings.recommendation: Add a test with price 19.99 and percent 10, expecting 17.99.

findings.title: Recommend a negative-price behavior test
findings.description: Price is not validated; a negative price with a valid percent currently returns a negative discounted amount. Test documents this behavior rather than assuming intent.
findings.recommendation: Add a characterization test for negative price input and confirm whether rejection is desired.

findings.title: Recommend boundary-equality tests for clamp
findings.description: Supplied tests exercise values below/above the range and inside it, but not value equal to lower or upper, where max/min ties should return that bound unchanged.
findings.recommendation: Add a parameterized boundary test asserting equality to lower and upper is preserved.

findings.title: Recommend a behavior test for inverted bounds
findings.description: With lower greater than upper the nested min/max silently returns lower. Intent is unclear; pinning current behavior documents it.
findings.recommendation: Test clamp with lower > upper to record the current result or assert a documented ValueError if that is intended.
suggested_tests: test_inverted_bounds: inputs=clamp(5, 10, 0); expected=10 (current) or ValueError if intent is validation

findings.title: Recommend a non-numeric input test
findings.description: Passing None or strings triggers comparison TypeError from min/max; a test can confirm the failure mode.
findings.recommendation: Add a test asserting a TypeError is raised for None value.

findings.title: Recommend a None-input test
findings.description: parse_port passes value directly to int; None is not in the supplied parameter set, and int(None) raises TypeError before the range check.
findings.recommendation: Add a None case asserting the current TypeError behavior, distinct from the range ValueError.

findings.title: Recommend an empty-string test
findings.description: An empty string is a distinct malformed input from the supplied 'bad' case; int('') raises ValueError during conversion, before the range check.
findings.recommendation: Add an empty-string case asserting the current conversion ValueError.

findings.title: Recommend an exact exception-type test for out-of-range ports
findings.description: The supplied invalid-value test accepts either ValueError or TypeError, so a regression to TypeError for an out-of-range port would still pass.
findings.recommendation: Narrow an out-of-range test to expect ValueError only.
suggested_tests: test_invalid_range_error_type: inputs='0'; expected=ValueError('invalid port'), not TypeError

findings.title: Recommend importing first_item in the test module
findings.description: Supplied tests call first_item without importing it, so tests would fail with NameError before checking behavior.
findings.recommendation: Add an import of first_item in the test module using the project's import path before test definitions.
suggested_tests: test_first_item_imported: inputs=first_item imported from module under test; expected=first_item(['a']) == 'a'

findings.title: Recommend non-empty tuple and string input tests
findings.description: Existing behavior returns the first element/character for any subscriptable non-empty sequence; tests exercise only a list.
findings.recommendation: Add parameterized cases for a one-element tuple and a non-empty string.

findings.title: Recommend empty tuple and string input tests
findings.description: Empty lists raise IndexError in the supplied tests; empty tuple and empty string follow the same indexing behavior.
findings.recommendation: Add parameterized empty-sequence cases expecting IndexError.

findings.title: Recommend non-subscriptable input tests
findings.description: Passing a non-subscriptable value triggers TypeError from indexing; current tests do not exercise malformed input types.
findings.recommendation: Add parameterized None and integer inputs expecting TypeError.

findings.title: Recommend an empty-file test
findings.description: An empty UTF-8 file is a valid boundary case; read should return an empty string.
findings.recommendation: Add a case that writes zero bytes and asserts an empty string result.
suggested_tests: test_empty_file_returns_empty_string: inputs=path to a 0-byte UTF-8 file; expected=load_text(path) == ''

findings.title: Recommend an invalid-UTF-8 input test
findings.description: Malformed bytes that are not valid UTF-8 should raise UnicodeDecodeError during read.
findings.recommendation: Add a case with invalid byte sequences and assert UnicodeDecodeError.

findings.title: Recommend a None-path test
findings.description: Passing None as path exercises input validation behavior; open should raise TypeError.
findings.recommendation: Add a negative test for None and assert TypeError.

findings.title: Recommend a directory-path test
findings.description: A directory path is a malformed file input; open should raise IsADirectoryError.
findings.recommendation: Add a case using tmp_path itself as the path and assert IsADirectoryError.

findings.title: Recommend a None-percent error test
findings.description: Supplied tests exercise numeric out-of-range percents, but not None. Current comparison behavior raises TypeError rather than ValueError.
findings.recommendation: Add a malformed-input test documenting current None-percent behavior.

findings.title: Recommend a None-price error test
findings.description: Supplied tests use numeric price values only. A None price reaches arithmetic and raises TypeError.
findings.recommendation: Add a malformed-input test documenting current None-price behavior.

findings.title: Recommend a zero-price boundary test
findings.description: Supplied tests use price=10. Zero price is a distinct boundary input for the discount calculation.
findings.recommendation: Add a zero-price case to confirm the result remains zero after rounding.
